name: SHARP in-network reduction only helps all-reduce, not all-to-all or all-gather
symptom: SHARP in-network reduction is often described as accelerating 'collective communication', but it only accelerates all-reduce operations. All-to-all (used in MoE expert-parallel) and all-gather do not benefit from SHARP.
root_cause: SHARP performs reduction operations inside the switch. All-reduce is the only common collective that is a pure reduction. All-gather and all-to-all are data movement operations that cannot be reduced inside the switch. MoE models use all-to-all for expert-parallel routing, which does not benefit from SHARP.
workaround: For MoE models, SHARP provides limited benefit. Focus on network bandwidth and latency for all-to-all operations. For dense models with tensor-parallel, SHARP provides significant benefit for all-reduce.
notes: This is an important distinction for MoE models. The marketing around SHARP and in-network computing often implies broad collective acceleration, but the actual benefit is limited to all-reduce. MoE expert-parallel all-to-all remains a network-bound operation.
